name: FILM
plain: FILM (Reda et al., Google, ECCV 2022): makes the middle frame between two video frames, also for large motion, from a flow pyramid in both directions and features shared across scales. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: FILM (Reda et al., ECCV 2022): frame interpolation for large motion, the authors' film_net with the Style weights (the published default) as dajes/frame-interpolation-pytorch ports it. A 7-level image pyramid of both frames, cascaded features (one convolutional sub-tree extractor shared by all levels, so the coarse levels learn from fine training samples), a residual flow pyramid in both directions with one predictor shared by the coarse levels, both frames' images and features warped to the time on the 5 finest levels, and a U-Net-like decoder. Trained for the middle frame; other times run as upstream allows.

papers.title: FILM: Frame Interpolation for Large Motion

task_io: Input: two RGB images (consecutive frames). Output: the frame between them at `timestep` (0.5 by default; 0 = the first, 1 = the second), RGB in [0, 1].

quality.title: DAVIS 2017 480p, 2 frame triplets per video (180), PSNR / SSIM
quality.protocol: DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 5e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.001 and p99 <= 0.005 (absolute error of the output `frame`).
